question: What typed event, if any, does each document carry, as a row that is numeric by construction?

contract.prompt_hash_covers: wire system prompt + user template + canonical schema
contract.language_pin: applied CENTRALLY in model_provider.complete, never at this call site; wire_system() shows the pinned text
contract.no_event_is_not_a_refusal: a no_event row is a SUCCESSFUL classification and is written like any other row -- it is how L2 measures the corpus's genuine event rate, and dropping it would make the denominator silently wrong
contract.one_row_per_document: spec section 2.4: the DOMINANT event only. v1's schema has no multi-event shape, and additionalProperties:false forbids smuggling one in

vocabulary.source: docs/research_notes/2026-09-11/spec_events_and_calibration.md sections 1.2 (v1's TABLE; the section's closing sentence miscounts by one) and 1.2b (v2's analyst-action addendum)
vocabulary.no_fourth_direction: There is no value for 'I do not know'. A genuinely uncertain call commits to the best-guess sign AND sets `confidence` low. Cohen's kappa cannot be computed over a set that includes an escape hatch one rater uses more than the other.
vocabulary.confidence: `confidence` in [0, 1] is the model's stated probability that the emitted (event_type, direction) PAIR, taken together, is the correct reading of the document. It is NOT `event_intel.extraction.tier`, which is a PARSE-FIDELITY judgment (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/FAILED) barred by the D4 closure ruling from being read as an outcome probability. This one IS allowed to be read as a probability, because inter-rater kappa is the external check that catches a reader free-lancing high confidence.

kappa_protocol.magnitude_bucket: weighted kappa, ordinal over MAGNITUDE_BUCKETS, LINEAR weights
kappa_protocol.confidence: mean absolute difference -- it is continuous, so kappa does not apply
kappa_protocol.sample: the SAME rows under both prompts; the spec's control is 500 rows

corpus.stratified_axes: month of the PIT anchor x symbol-frequency quartile, largest-remainder allocation, np.random.default_rng(seed)
corpus.dedupe: one typing per DISTINCT TEXT, fanned back out at join time to every (symbol, entry_date) panel row carrying it; 340,465 rows over 163,288 texts is 2.08x
corpus.eligibility: every row the panel holds. The label-source filter is the CORPUS's rule and was already applied by the panel builder; re-applying it on the panel's own feed spellings would drop rows silently

tokens.prefix_cache_note: the SAME tokens are sent either way -- what a prefix cache changes is the RATE on the 1432-token system prefix, which is byte-identical across every call. The two cost columns are the same token count at two rates, not two token counts

calibration_against_the_ledger.reading: the measured rows were CORPUS documents, whose bodies run to the 2,000-char cap, and they still came in BELOW this panel estimate -- so 4 chars/token over-states the real tokenizer on this system prompt and every cost column here is conservative

tokens.caveat: 4.0 chars/token is a CONVENTION, not a tokenizer. The only honest anchor is the ledger, and it is printed beside it

cost.repo_rates_source: backend/config.LLM_PRICE_PER_MTOK -- DERIVED from the provider's own balance ledger; this is what llm_telemetry bills every row at
cost.measured_caveat: `cached_tokens` was 0 on every one of the 7,565 rows, so the measured $/row credits NO prefix cache. It is therefore an UPPER bound for a run that gets one, and the reconciliation against the provider's balance stays scripts/llm_cost_audit.py

cap.note: at the measured $/row this run is $6.30 against a $8.00 cap -- the cap does not bind

one_row_per_document: a document tagged with several tickers is scoped to the FIRST and carries the rest; fanning it into N rows would multiply one reading into N correlated ones

concurrency.order: results are collected and flushed in SUBMISSION order; the cursor never passes a unit whose predecessors are unwritten

cap.usd_per_row_source: THIS RUN's own ledger rows (19884 calls)
cap.checked: before every submission, against the ledger total refreshed every 100 rows
cap.also_in_force: lab_budget's UTC-DAY cap, but only on the `--reader` path (lab_reader.resolve); a direct `--backend deepseek` run is capped by --max-usd alone

protocol.magnitude_bucket: weighted kappa, ordinal over MAGNITUDE_BUCKETS, LINEAR weights
protocol.confidence: mean absolute difference -- it is continuous, so kappa does not apply
protocol.sample: the SAME rows under both prompts; the spec's control is 500 rows

usage.cost_source: the CALL LEDGER, not a local cost field

ledger.note: a list-price reconstruction from the call ledger, not a bill. `scripts/llm_cost_audit.py --snapshot` reconciles against the provider's own balance and is the ground truth

manifest.what: one typed row per corpus document, L2's frozen vocabulary. The .jsonl files are DATA and are gitignored; this manifest is tracked.

verdict: 19,996 rows typed from panel, 4 refused (REFUSED_SCHEMA=4), event_type kappa 0.6661 on 50 re-prompted rows; $6.4370 by the ledger
headline: 19,996 typed / 20,000 read from panel at 8 workers; 69.0% no_event; refusal rate 0.0002; $6.44
next_test: E1 on these typed rows against E1 on the keyword proxy, same panel, same splits, same three controls -- the only changed variable being how the events were typed
